content:
toni: quick report from onboarding tests: webhook-sample created duplicate orders when token refresh and client retry overlapped. reproducible in staging.

ash: can you share the minimal trace?

toni: sure:
```
[2076543210] POST /orders -> 401 token_expired
[2076543211] app: immediate retry (no idempotency header)
[2076543212] sdk: token refresh attempt 1 -> 429
[2076543215] sdk: refresh attempt 2 -> 200
[2076543216] both retries reach backend -> two orders created
```

marco: root cause = two independent retry paths + missing idempotency signal. we need a small set of coordinated mitigations.

ash: proposal: 1) sample apps must attach Idempotency-Key for mutating endpoints (example code + test) 2) align sdks to use full_jitter for refresh backoff (node/go/py) 3) add an opt-in short "replay_guard" that suppresses sdk resend when a recent identical request was just sent (default window 250ms, opt-in until validated).

toni: for the sample app I added a tiny debounce (uniform random 80-280ms) before client retry and that prevented duplicates in our runs. will push that change.

marco: implementation note: generated idempotency keys should be weak (request-hash + short nonce) and only used for short replay suppression. never generate strong long-lived keys unless app opts in. document parity across sdks with flag `sdk.replay_guard.enabled` and `refresh.backoff.strategy=full_jitter`.

ash: telemetry: emit metrics `sdk.replay_guard.suppressed` and `platform.duplicate_events.count`. also log suppressed events with request-hash to facilitate debugging.

docs-bot: added task DOCS-812 to update onboarding guide with idempotency examples for Node/Python/Go.

toni: followups: ash will open sdk PR to add replay_guard flag and backoff parity; i'll update sample app and add an integration test that asserts a single backend create in the repro harness.

ash: will target a canary release; include unit tests for backoff math and an integration test simulating refresh 429 + app retry.

marco: agreed. one caution: ensure multi-instance apps aren't masked by weak keys. suppression window should be conservative and opt-in by default. after some telemetry we can consider enabling by default.

toni: thanks all — logging RW-6001 (sdk replay guard + parity) and RW-6002 (sample app idempotency test). closing the thread. :white_check_mark:
